amendments.rule: Where the ASV's recasting leaves a preposition with no English word — the impersonal `קרא לְ` + suffix rendered as a personal passive, `וְקֹרָא לָךְ` → *and thou shalt be called*, or a dative `לְ` + suffix rendered as a bare English indirect object, `תְּנָה לִּי` → *give me* — the preposition is its own `unrepresented` unit and its suffix takes the English pronoun that realizes it, including a subject pronoun. This is rule 21's recasting clause outside the resultative `הָיָה לְ`, and it is the case where rule 18's *possessive or object* is not the whole range. **The `לְ` is the commonest case, not the condition.** The same recasting silences any preposition it leaves nothing to say: `צוּר עַל` → *besieged Tirzah* and `צִוִּיתִי עָלֶיךָ` → *commanded thee* leave `עַל` bare, `אֶל` goes the same way before a bare English object, and a `בְּ` whose object the ASV promotes to a direct object — *blew the trumpet* — keeps nothing either. Read the condition, not the lemma: ask whether the ASV spends an English word on what that preposition contributes. **And a word the ASV writes as part of a neighbouring morpheme's own compound rendering is not a word spent on the preposition.** Where a Hebrew adverb or noun standing beside the preposition is rendered by an English expression written in two or three words, that expression belongs whole to the morpheme it renders, exactly as rule 30 reads its one-English-word condition as one rendering rather than one token, and the preposition takes a word only where the ASV has written one for its own relation. `הֶחָצֵר סָבִיב לַמִּשְׁכָּן` → *the court round about the tabernacle* gives *round about* whole to `סָבִיב`, headed on *round* under rule 24, and leaves the `לְ` `unrepresented`, exactly as the coordinated `וְלַמִּזְבֵּחַ` beside it is left. Do not divide such an expression to give a present preposition something to hold: rule 11 gives each morpheme the English it licenses, and half of another morpheme's fixed rendering is not English this one licenses. Test by subtraction as elsewhere — drop the word and ask whether the preposition's own relation has gone unstated, or whether only the neighbouring expression has been broken in two. The corpus renders `סָבִיב` by *round about* headed on *round* in 144 units and by a bare *round* in two, one of them hedged and the other a doubled adverb for which the ASV writes a separate word for each occurrence, and it reads the whole compound as the adverb's own in four of the five units where a determined preposition follows it.
amendments.why: EXO.40 analysed the same ASV compound two ways — EXO.40.8 gave *round about* whole to סָבִיב, EXO.40.33 gave *round* to סָבִיב and *about* to the following לַ — and nothing in the contract as it stood decided between them. Rule 11's grant of the English a morpheme licenses pulls toward feeding a present preposition the second word, and rule 30's one-rendering reading pulls the other way, but rule 30 speaks to morphemes inside the expression rather than a neighbour outside it. Rule 40 is the rule that decides when a preposition holds nothing, so the qualification belongs in its text rather than as a new rule pointing back at it. The corpus carries it: 144 units to two on the adverb, 4 to 1 in the exact environment where a determined preposition follows, and only three units in the whole corpus align a לְ to *about*, one of which is the single hedged unit that split the pair. That outlier names its own competing reading, so the precedent is one-sided rather than self-contradictory. The addition changes no existing sentence of rule 40 and reuses the subtraction test the rule already relies on.

conventions: The Piel כָּהַן is rendered *minister in the priest's office*, and the whole English expression is one unit on that verb, headed on *minister* rather than on *priest's*: the office phrase is the idiom's own body and not a light verb's complement under rule 44. Its supplied subject pronoun and modal stay with it under rule 17, and the unit is discontinuous around the dative *unto me*, whose two words belong to the לְ and its suffix (rules 18, 25). EXO.40.13 and EXO.40.15 are read alike; each verse's note names the competing head.

Where the hiphil of לָבֵשׁ is recast so that the garments become the English direct object and the person clothed is reached by *upon*, the object marker standing on the person takes that *upon* under rule 16's first family, and heads on it. EXO.40.13 gives *upon* to the marker on אַהֲרֹן and leaves the second marker, standing on the garments the ASV writes bare, unrepresented; EXO.40.14 gives *upon* to the marker on the suffixed object while the suffix takes *them*. This is the reading to carry into the parallel investiture formulas.

Where עָרַךְ and its cognate noun עֵרֶךְ both stand in one clause, each morpheme takes one English expression, and which of them carries *in order* follows from what the other's own rendering leaves rather than from a fixed preference. EXO.40.4 gives *the things* to the suffixed עֶרְכּוֹ, so *set in order* is the verb's light-verb rendering headed on *order* (rule 44); EXO.40.23 gives *the bread* to the rectum לֶחֶם, so *in order* is the construct עֵרֶךְ's own adverbial rendering (rule 33) and the verb keeps *set*. The divergence is the ASV's and is not a split.

EXO.40.2 and EXO.40.17 write the same בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ, but the ASV collapses 40.2's two date phrases into the single *On the first day of the first month*, so that verse's second בְּ, its לַ, its assimilated article and its second חֹדֶשׁ are unrepresented under rules 22 and 40, while 40.17 renders each of them. In 40.2 the two written ordinals are distributed one to אֶחָד and one to רִאשׁוֹן, each standing beside the noun it modifies in English; the reverse distribution is defensible and is named in that unit's note. A later reader should expect the candidate table to flag this pair and should not read it as a divergence of analysis.

report: One real cross-verse split, patched in EXO.40.33: סָבִיב → *round about*. EXO.40.8 gives the whole compound to the adverb; EXO.40.33 gave *round* to סָבִיב and *about* to the following לַ. The corpus answers settle it against the split — 144 units read סָבִיב as *round about* headed on *round*, against two bare *round*s (1KI.18.35, itself hedged and naming the competing reading, and EZK.37.2, a doubled adverb for which the ASV genuinely writes two words); restricted to סָבִיב followed by a determined preposition, precedent runs 4 to 1 for the whole compound; and לְ → *about* exists in only three corpus units, one of them that same hedged 1KI.18.35. In the patch s006 takes t007 t008 and s007 goes unrepresented, exactly as the coordinated second לַ (s011) already was.

Checked and found licensed rather than split: the בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ date formula (EXO.40.2 vs 40.17 — the ASV collapses the two Hebrew date phrases into one English phrase in 40.2, so its second בְּ, its לַ, its assimilated article and its second חֹדֶשׁ are unrepresented under rules 22 and 40, while 40.17 renders each); the cognate עָרַךְ/עֵרֶךְ pair in 40.4 and 40.23; אֵת → *upon* under the recast hiphil of לָבֵשׁ in 40.13 and 40.14; article placement across construct chains (rules 28, 29, 47); the article before מַיִם unrepresented in 40.12 against rendered in 40.20 and 40.25; and the varying renderings of נָתַן, שׂים, עָלָה, קוּם, לְ, בְּ and עַל, each of which follows what the ASV wrote.

BSB: no genuine error among the 19 disagreements. Every one falls in a documented convention family — the לֵאמֹר lamed (rule 27), the repeated בֵּין in 40.7 and 40.30 (rule 26), עַל silenced by recasting in 40.3 and 40.21 (rule 40), agreement articles on ordinals in 40.2 and 40.17 (rule 47), object markers (rule 16), and rule 22 repetitions (חֹדֶשׁ in 40.2, הְיֹת in 40.15, the second לַ in 40.33). The patch adds one further disagreement of that same kind at WLC.EXO.40.33.007; that is the correct outcome, not a cost to be avoided.

The chapter's single `added` unit — *wherewith* at EXO.40.30 — was re-examined and stands. The לְ before רָחְצָה already holds the written *to* (corpus: לְ before an infinitive construct aligns to a written *to* in 583 units and records no *wherewith to*), and no relative or resumptive morpheme stands in the clause, so the relative adverb answers to nothing (rules 30, 55). The unit note already names the competing reading.
All three evidence requests were answered; nothing is left outstanding. Four conventions recorded and one amendment returned, to rule 40.
